correctness.rationale: For A=diag(1,-1) and B=eps[[0,1],[1,0]], explicit orthogonal rotation yields loss 2 sin²(2alpha)+2 eps² cos²(2alpha), minimized at 2eps². The eigenbasis of the Gaussian pencil has loss 2eps²/(cos²theta+eps² sin²theta), theta uniform unsigned Gaussian angle. Monotonicity maps best of L trials to the minimum order statistic with density 2L/pi (1-2theta/pi)^(L-1). The exact expectation follows. T=tan(theta) gives E[L1]=2eps; the endpoint u=pi/2-theta has a uniform O(1) comparison for L2 to integral u/(u²+eps²), yielding 16/pi² eps² log(1/eps). The L>=3 rescaled integrand is dominated by u^(L-3), integrable; L=3 integrates to 48 log2/pi². Thus precisely three trials are necessary and sufficient for bounded expected squared-loss/optimum ratio on THIS matrix family, not across all algorithms or families. Independently evaluated quadrature at eps 0.1, 0.02 and 0.005 corroborates divergent L1/L2 ratios and finite L3 ratio; source rational and eigenbasis code was inspected without relying on its success marker.
residual_risks: The conclusion is for a specific real 2x2 Gaussian best-of-L orthogonal eigenbasis algorithm and expected SQUARED off-diagonal Frobenius loss, not unsquared error, all instances, floating-point computation or optimal general restart complexity.
